Commentary.Commentary: See you then! All eyes now shift to the main tournament. The Men in Green will look to hit the ground running when they face the Netherlands in their campaign opener on Saturday, the 7th of February at 5.30 am GMT. Meanwhile, Ireland has a big test awaiting them as they prepare to lock horns with Sri Lanka on Sunday, the 8th of February at 1.30 pm GMT. It is a damp end to the day, but the real action is just around the corner. Do join us then. Cheers!

What to expect? With both sides using this game to sharpen their combinations and test match-ups ahead of the global tournament, this warm-up has all the ingredients of a competitive, high-intensity contest rather than a gentle tune-up, especially with Ireland eager to measure themselves against one of the most in-form sides in world cricket.

Ireland's growing belief - Ireland, however, bring their own sense of purpose after a 2-0 series win over UAE, where their batting showed improved composure and their bowling found consistency. Paul Stirling continues to be the heartbeat at the top, with Harry Tector's elegance and Curtis Campher's all-round impact adding balance through the middle, while Lorcan Tucker provides explosiveness behind the stumps. With the ball, Mark Adair and Josh Little give Ireland genuine pace and movement up front, backed by the accuracy of Barry McCarthy and the control of spinners like George Dockrell and Ben White, giving them more variety than in previous seasons.

Pakistan's bowling-led dominance - Pakistan's whitewash of Australia was built on ruthless control with the ball, especially through their spinners, who strangled the Aussie batting unit so effectively that not a single batter managed a half-century across the series. The final game, in particular, was a brutal display of dominance, handing Australia their heaviest defeat by runs in T20Is and underlining just how well this side has found its rhythm. With Salman Agha leading a squad packed with depth, Pakistan have multiple avenues to hurt the opposition. Babar Azam, Fakhar Zaman, Saim Ayub and Sahibzada Farhan provide a blend of experience and aggression at the top, while Shadab Khan, Mohammad Nawaz and Abrar Ahmed give Pakistan a formidable spin attack that can take over games in the middle overs. Add the pace and late swing of Shaheen Shah Afridi and Naseem Shah, and Pakistan look like a side built for tournament conditions.

World Cup warm-up begins - The road to the 2026 T20 World Cup begins to heat up as Pakistan and Ireland lock horns in a high-quality warm-up that promises far more than just a routine practice game. Fresh from a statement home series against Australia, Pakistan arrive brimming with confidence and clarity, while Ireland come in quietly confident after building momentum of their own in recent weeks.
